A.basis: [A] per-item human review: 30% of grants touched by a person; no AI; more paper and contacts
A.name: Traditional human-centred operation

A8.basis: Adversarial correction ADV-B-005: A with the same exception incidence as the other approaches; the 30% per-item-review assumption in A is a separate, unmeasured lever
A8.name: Traditional operation, same exception definition as B-D (8%)

AL.basis: [A] A's human workflows, but technology bought at the same licence as C; isolates the workflow effect from the build-versus-buy effect
AL.name: Traditional human-centred operation on licensed software

B.basis: OM1 levers (parameters.json): exception-based review, AI assistance, same processes
B.name: Existing workflow enhanced with AI

C.basis: OM2/OM3 levers; Unbound licence; per-sponsor decision teams (SPD-ADV-001, SPD-ADV-004)
C.name: AI-native redesign on Unbound

C0.basis: Adversarial correction ADV-B-006: C's platform, licence and per-sponsor teams with B's workflow parameters (no determination reuse, no minute/contact/reconciliation/complex-hour reductions)
C0.name: Unbound without unmeasured redesign levers

D.basis: [A] removes convention-only recurring obligations, default-ACH, proactive notices; legal obligations retained
D.name: AI-native redesign plus elimination of convention-only activities

meta.basis: simplification model.py + decision_teams.py unchanged; assumptions in this file are [A]

complex_policy.basis: OD-M-09 (owner decision): complex assets are rare and are sold on receipt by a contracted intermediary, so internal handling is intake checks and proceeds reconciliation (1 hour [A]) and the complex share is a quarter of the earlier mix assumption [A]. Applied to every approach, so it is a business policy, not an Unbound-only lever; the intermediary fee stays fund-borne.

E1.basis: daf-landscape business model D2C; market mix from parameters.json
E1.name: Independent national DAF sponsor (direct to donor)

E2.basis: [S] DAFRC FY2024 panel, 802 community foundations: median 46, p75 128, p90 313 DAFs; only 7 hold >=1,500 (daf-landscape data/mission-2026-11-14/dafrc-sponsor-schedule-d-fy2019-2024.csv); non-DAF programs excluded
E2.name: Community foundation (DAF program inside a broader foundation)

E3.basis: daf-landscape advisor-distribution model; release 1 has no advisor-managed program and no fund-paid advisor compensation (CNV-GRT-009), so release-1 revenue is the sponsor admin fee only; advisor_sponsored is a later option
E3.name: Wealth-management and advisor-distributed DAF provider

E4.basis: daf-landscape high-volume-low-balance and embedded models; employer pays acquisition
E4.name: High-volume workplace giving provider

E5.basis: daf-landscape outsourced-admin/white-label; decisions stay with each sponsor (SPD-ADV-001)
E5.name: Enterprise outsourced DAF administrator serving many sponsors

licence.basis: [A] Unbound's vendor cost per account (decision_teams.license_floors) at the stated whole-platform scale, plus markup. Scales corrected after adversarial review ADV-B-001: the US market holds at most ~737k traditional invested DAF accounts and only 20 sponsors hold >=5,000 (DAFRC FY2024); 1M is kept only as a labelled reference.

staffed_assumptions.basis: [A] floor of 4 FTE for coverage and segregation of duties; 15% supervision overhead; Unbound staff prepare half of exception and complex-gift work while sponsors' own appointed people decide (SPD-ADV-001). [market-data] Ren administration $413-745 per DAF-year and iPhi software $32-129 per DAF-year from Form 990 contractor payments (report 13; floors, may bundle services not modelled such as gift consulting).

vendor_assumptions.basis: [A] build_capex from parameters.json amortised over 5 years; sales and implementation per new sponsor; 20% of sponsors new each year. Sponsor onboarding cost is already in the vendor floor (sponsor_level:platform_service).
